Hi Lina (and Arjun),

Great questions — thank you. Attached is a compact proposal (Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v3.pdf) and a split-sheet that shows how we’d model your 60/30/10 traffic profile with a single global commit. High-level answers below:

- Single global commit: Yes — we can do one global commit that you allocate by region in the contract annex. This avoids managing three separate commits. The commit gives you a blended committed rate (per-token) based on the committed volume.

- Regional allocation & true-ups: You declare the initial target split (60/30/10) in the MA. We perform monthly actuals and true-ups. If a region exceeds its allocated portion, overage handling follows the tier rules: overages are charged at the committed tier rate up to the next tier threshold for that month; beyond your committed volume, excess usage is billed at the published on-demand per-token rate. Example: if committed tier is 500M tokens/month at $0.0006/token and EU spikes such that total across regions exceeds 500M, the excess tokens are billed at on-demand $0.0010/token (see attached).

- Proration: We prorate commits monthly, not hourly. Unused committed tokens do not carry forward beyond the monthly true-up (we can discuss carry-forward if needed for procurement).

- Invoicing & VAT: We support issuing invoices in EUR to your EU entity and will include VAT handling where applicable. For multi-entity customers we can split invoices by entity/region; this is an ops setup but common.

- Data residency: Region routing is supported; EU traffic can be pinned to EU-serving infrastructure. That controls where inference happens (and therefore TOS/data residency language).

Next steps: if this model looks good I’ll loop in Markus (sales ops) and Neha (finance) to lock the exact tier pricing and currency mechanics, then share a redline-friendly MA annex and a DocuSign link.

Camila — short answers and suggested language below. I copied Neha for invoicing specifics.

Pricing table (6-month commit, example):
- 250M–499M tokens/month: $0.00075/token (committed)
- 500M–999M tokens/month: $0.00060/token (committed)
- 1B+ tokens/month: $0.00045/token (committed)
Public on-demand: $0.00100/token

Overage mechanics (proposed procurement-friendly wording):
"Committed volume is applied globally each month. If total account usage for the month exceeds the committed volume, additional tokens will be billed at the public on-demand rate of $0.00100/token. Within the committed volume, regional deviations are not charged extra — the committed volume is pooled and consumed across regions."

Follow-up: if you'd like to guarantee a minimum regional floor (e.g., minimum 200M for EU), we can add a regional guaranteed allocation (treated as a soft floor) which would reduce overall flexibility and may change blended pricing.

Invoicing & VAT (Neha): we can emit invoices to the EU legal entity and include VAT handling. For now we route billing from a single Redwood master account but can produce a separate invoice for the EU entity as an ops workstream and include the EU VAT line. Currency: we can invoice in EUR; rates are fixed per-month on invoice.

Neha — can you confirm any latency on setting up separate-entity invoicing and call out any minimum lead-time for accounting?

— Markus
